title: Inertial synchronization of networked oscillators in arbitrary dimensions
authors: Kirill Kovalenko, Bruce X. Dai, Fanshu Fang, Zerong Guo, Haoran Liu, Federico Botta, Charo I. del Genio, Stefano Boccaletti, Simona Olmi
abstract: The Kuramoto model provides a paradigmatic framework for studying synchronization of interacting oscillators, and has been generalized to arbitrary dimensions to describe swarms, flocks and multi-dimensional opinion dynamics. Yet, existing formulations neglect inertia, a key mechanism known to enhance information propagation and collective responsiveness. Here, we introduce and analyze an inertial Kuramoto model in arbitrary dimensions. We show that inertia fundamentally alters the nature of the synchronization transition, inducing a crossover from continuous to discontinuous behavior, with the onset of hysteresis depending explicitly on both inertia and dimensionality parity. Our analytical theory is supported by extensive numerical simulations. These results establish inertia as a crucial ingredient of high-dimensional collective dynamics and reveal a novel universal structure in synchronization phenomena.
summary: This work analyzes the inertial Kuramoto model in arbitrary dimensions to study collective synchronization. The key finding is that incorporating inertia fundamentally changes the synchronization transition, inducing hysteresis whose existence depends on the system's dimensionality and the magnitude of the inertia. This establishes inertia as a crucial control parameter for high-dimensional collective dynamics.
main_problem: The paper investigates the synchronization dynamics of networked oscillators in arbitrary dimensions, specifically focusing on the role of inertia.
main_result: Inertia fundamentally alters the synchronization transition, causing a crossover from continuous to discontinuous behavior, with the onset of hysteresis depending explicitly on both inertia and dimensionality parity.
method: The analysis combines analytical theory, deriving self-consistent equations for the order parameter, with extensive numerical simulations.
model_or_system: The system is modeled by an inertial Kuramoto model in $D$ dimensions, where the dynamics are governed by a generalized equation involving the second time derivative of the oscillator vectors.
key_observables: Order parameter ($R$), synchronization transition type (continuous vs. discontinuous), and the width of the hysteresis loop.

figures_summary: Figures illustrate the change in transition order (continuous vs. hysteretic) with inertia and dimension, and show the time evolution of the order parameter across different synchronization regimes.
paper_structure: The paper develops the inertial Kuramoto model, derives mean-field equations, analyzes the transition points using stability criteria, and compares the resulting synchronization behavior across various dimensions and inertia regimes.
why_interesting: The study of collective dynamics, phase transitions, and emergent order parameters in high-dimensional systems is highly relevant to understanding complex quantum many-body systems and open quantum systems.
